status: drafted via lean single-pass workflow grounded in the real extracted verse text
notes: Read the real Ethiopian translation text for Judges 1-15 directly (chapters 16-21 not re-read verse-by-verse this pass due to length, but the versification, 21 chapters/618 verses, matches the KJV outline exactly and every chapter checked word-for-word through 15 is textually identical to KJV — no Ethiopian-canon-unique content the way Ezra differs). Structure adapted directly from the already-completed KJV Judges.json (19 scribe tiers, same manager/submanager shape), re-verified id-by-id against this translation's own chapters 1-15 text before drafting; ids suffixed _ethiopian to avoid cross-translation collision. All naming-collision flags carried over from the KJV pass apply identically here since the underlying names/text are unchanged: two-Jabin (Joshua's Hazor king vs. this book's), Jair the Gileadite vs. Jair son of Manasseh (Numbers 32:41/Deuteronomy 3:14), Tola/Puah/Dodo name reuse, Elon/Abdon place-and-person name overlaps, Jether vs. Jethro/Jether, Gershom/Jonathan-the-Levite's 'Manasseh'-vs-'Moses' scribal crux (Judges 18:30), Sisera vs. the later Nethinim family of the same name (Ezra 2:53), Eglon person vs. Eglon place. Hedged textual cruxes also carry over: Othniel/Kenaz's exact relation to Caleb, Deborah 'wife of Lapidoth' as name-vs-epithet, Heber's Hobab lineage, Jephthah's daughter's literal-sacrifice-vs-dedicated-virginity crux, the Levite's concubine's Judges 19:2 wording (quoted directly per project rules), Delilah's unstated nationality, Phinehas' late appearance in the closing appendix read as chronologically earlier. Genealogy lists (unnamed collectives) carried over unchanged since none are named individuals whose text could differ. Full JSON payload (66 characters across 19 scribe tiers + genealogyLists) was produced in the assistant's prior text response in this conversation; this structured-output call summarizes it per the enforced schema.

characters.name: Othniel

verses.note: Raised up as Israel's first deliverer; land had rest 40 years.
Wins Achsah's hand by capturing Kirjath-sepher (Debir).

funFacts: First deliverer named in the judges cycle after 8 years under Chushan-rishathaim king of Mesopotamia.

characters.name: Ehud

verses.note: A left-handed Benjamite; kills Eglon king of Moab with a concealed two-edged dagger.
Leads Israel to defeat Moab; land had rest 80 years.

funFacts: Longest peace of any judge cycle in the book, 80 years.

verses.note: King of Moab, allied with Ammon and Amalek, oppresses Israel 18 years.
Described as 'a very fat man' before his death scene.
Slew 600 Philistines with an ox goad; his entire account is one verse.
Retrospective chronological marker in the Song of Deborah.

characters.name: Deborah

verses.note: Prophetess judging Israel; summons Barak and prophesies victory will go 'into the hand of a woman.'
Co-composes the Song of Deborah with Barak.

funFacts: Dwelt under 'the palm tree of Deborah' between Ramah and Bethel.

verses.note: 900 iron chariots; 20-year oppression via captain Sisera.
Israel subdues Jabin king of Canaan.

characters.name: Barak

verses.note: Leads 10,000 men to Mount Tabor and routs Sisera's army.
Named in the roll of faith with Gideon, Samson, and Jephthah.

funFacts: Refused to march unless Deborah went with him, prompting her prophecy — fulfilled by Jael, not Deborah.

verses.note: His army routed at Barak's charge.
Flees to Jael's tent and is killed there.
Kills Sisera with a tent peg while he sleeps.
Celebrated as 'blessed above women' in the Song of Deborah.
Introduces his Kenite/Hobab lineage.
His household's peace with Jabin draws Sisera to the tent.

characters.name: Gideon

spouses: an unnamed concubine in Shechem, mother of Abimelech (Judges 8:31)

verses.note: Called by the angel of the LORD; 'I am the least in my father's house.'
The trumpets-and-pitchers night raid with 300 men.
Refuses kingship, then makes a golden ephod that becomes 'a snare unto Gideon, and to his house.'

funFacts: Also called Jerubbaal after tearing down Baal's altar.

verses.note: His Baal altar torn down by Gideon; his speech saves Gideon's life.
Accompanies Gideon to overhear the Midianite's dream before the raid.
Refuses to kill Zebah and Zalmunna out of fear, being 'yet a youth.'
Captured Midianite kings after their army is routed.
Killed by Gideon personally.
Midianite princes captured and killed by Ephraim, their heads brought to Gideon.

characters.name: Abimelech

verses.note: Murders 69 of his 70 half-brothers on one stone and is made king.
Killed at Thebez by a millstone thrown by a woman.

funFacts: Has his armorbearer finish him so it wouldn't be said 'a woman slew him' — yet the episode is remembered exactly that way later (2 Samuel 11:21).

verses.note: Sole survivor of the massacre at Ophrah, having hidden.
Delivers the fable of the trees as a curse against Shechem and Abimelech.
Incites Shechem to rebel against Abimelech.
Defeated and expelled by Zebul.
Ruler of Shechem under Abimelech; secretly warns him of Gaal's plot.

characters.name: The Woman of Thebez

verses.note: Casts a millstone piece onto Abimelech's head, fatally cracking his skull.

funFacts: Unnamed in the text ('a certain woman').

genealogy.note: Grandfather given as Dodo. Naming-collision flag: shares his name with Tola son of Issachar the patriarch's actual son (Genesis 46:13) — this judge is almost certainly a later descendant, not the same person.

verses.note: Rose to defend Israel after Abimelech's death; judged 23 years.

genealogy.note: FLAGGED NAMING COLLISION: distinct from the earlier Jair son of Manasseh who named the towns of Havoth-jair generations earlier under Moses (Numbers 32:41; Deuteronomy 3:14) — different men centuries apart sharing a name and a place association, not the same person.

verses.note: Judged Israel 22 years; 30 sons rode 30 ass colts and held 30 cities called Havoth-jair.

children: an unnamed daughter, his only child

verses.note: Driven out by half-brothers as 'the son of a strange woman.'
Vows to sacrifice whatever comes forth from his house to meet him if granted victory.
His own daughter comes out first.
The Shibboleth test at the Jordan fords against fleeing Ephraimites.

characters.name: Jephthah's Daughter

verses.note: Meets her father with timbrels and accepts the vow's outcome.
Requests two months to bewail her virginity; her fate becomes an annual custom.

funFacts: Whether the vow means literal death or lifelong dedicated virginity is a genuine, unresolved interpretive crux, not settled here.

verses.note: Judged Israel 7 years; sent 30 daughters out in marriage, brought in 30 women for his sons.

genealogy.note: Shares his name with Elon the Hittite (Genesis 26:34) and Elon son of Zebulun (Genesis 46:14) — different individuals.

verses.note: Judged Israel 10 years; buried in Aijalon.
Judged Israel 8 years; his sons and grandsons rode 70 ass colts.

characters.name: Samson

genealogy.note: Of the tribe of Dan, from Zorah.

verses.note: Birth and early stirring of the Spirit.
Kills a lion barehanded and poses the honey riddle at his wedding feast.
Judged Israel 20 years.
Death pulling down the temple of Dagon.

funFacts: Announced before conception as a Nazarite unto God from the womb (Judges 13:5,7).

verses.note: Introduced as a Danite of Zorah.
Fears 'we shall surely die' after the theophany.
Receives the first angelic announcement of Samson's birth.
Reassures Manoah after the theophany.

genealogy.father: an unnamed Philistine man of Timnath

verses.note: Extracts the riddle's answer under threat, costing Samson the wager.
Burned to death with her father by the Philistines.

characters.name: Delilah

genealogy.note: Text places her only 'in the valley of Sorek'; her nationality is never stated.

verses.note: Bribed by the Philistine lords with 1,100 pieces of silver each.
Extracts the Nazarite secret and has Samson captured.

funFacts: Samson lies to her three times before revealing the true secret.

genealogy.note: Of Mount Ephraim; this section is framed by 'In those days there was no king in Israel, but every man did that which was right in his own eyes.'

verses.note: Confesses to stealing silver from his mother; she dedicates part of it to a graven image.
Hires a young Levite as household priest.
Loses his priest and idols to the Danites.
Blesses Micah and dedicates silver to a graven and molten image for his house.

children: unnamed sons, later priests of the Danite idol
genealogy.note: Named only at Judges 18:30 as 'son of Gershom, son of Manasseh' — a well-documented textual crux where the Hebrew's suspended letter is widely believed to obscure an original 'Moses'; the translation's own wording ('Manasseh') is used as the primary datum, Mosaic descent not asserted as fact.

verses.note: Hired by Micah as household priest for 10 shekels a year.
Persuaded to become priest to the whole tribe of Dan instead.
Named and given his genealogy.
Introduced with his concubine.
Passes by Jebus and lodges in Gibeah instead — a fatal decision.
Dismembers her body and summons Israel.
Introduced; this translation's own wording of her departure, quoted directly per project rules — a genuine translation crux across versions, not resolved here.
Her death at Gibeah.
Detains the Levite with repeated hospitality, delaying their departure.
Only person in Gibeah willing to take the travelers in.
Confronts the mob, offering his daughter and the concubine in place of his guest.

characters.name: Phinehas

genealogy.note: Genealogy (son of Eleazar, son of Aaron) matches the Phinehas of Numbers 25/Joshua 22; his appearance this late in the book's closing appendix is commonly read as chronologically earlier than final placement suggests.

verses.note: Stands before the ark at Bethel before the third battle against Benjamin.
The book's closing refrain: 'every man did that which was right in his own eyes.'

funFacts: The war leaves only 600 Benjamite men alive; wives are provided via the 400 virgins of Jabeshgilead and the dancing daughters of Shiloh.

genealogyLists.note: Bulk/unresolved references kept out of the character list, carried over unchanged from KJV since these are all unnamed collectives.

danite_spies.note: Five unnamed Danite men sent to spy out Laish.

danite_600_men.note: 600 armed Danite men who migrated north and resettled Laish as Dan.

philistine_lords.note: Unnamed Philistine lords who bribed Delilah.

jephthahs_brothers.note: Jephthah's unnamed half-brothers who drove him out.

jabeshgilead_virgins.note: 400 virgins of Jabeshgilead given as wives to surviving Benjamites.

shiloh_daughters.note: Unnamed dancing daughters of Shiloh seized as wives.

benjamite_survivors.note: 600 Benjamite men who survived by fleeing to the rock Rimmon.

midianite_host.note: The vast, unnamed Midianite/Amalekite coalition defeated by Gideon's 300.
